text:
The evidence can't tell us whether timber harvest caused the loss.

What it does show: Hansen/UMD mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 within the asset (2.23% of its area). The loss is corroborated, since JRC's 2020 forest map agrees on 98% of the affected area and later years were observed through 2025.

The context is consistent with a plantation. The MGAP 2021 map classes 68.1 ha of the loss area as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), 13.2 ha as outside mapped forest, and none as native forest. That makes harvest plausible, but the map describes the setting, not the cause.

Hansen loss counts any stand replacement, including plantation cutting, fire, storm or clearing. So the data don't establish the cause, whether land use changed, legality, responsibility, or any compliance status. Confirming harvest would need other evidence, such as harvest records or management documents.
